name: Autosomal Dominant Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated focal hyperkeratotic plaques localized to palms and/or soles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis and absence of epidermolytic changes
Identification of pathogenic variant in associated keratin gene (e.g., KRT9 or KRT1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal palmoplantar keratoderma with autosomal dominant family history; genetic testing supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology and genetic testing aid in confirmation but clinical presentation and family history are primary.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in keratin genes such as KRT9 or KRT1 identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Family pedigree consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermolytic changes on histopathology
Mutations in KRT1 or KRT10 genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma beyond focal areas
Development of painful fissures impairing mobility
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or cellulitis
